42/G.goal: Explain how XR system implementation uses iterative prototyping and usability evaluation, and classify the prototype approaches used to test system designs before full implementation.
42/G.achieves: This supports the course aim of understanding and implementing an XR system with confidence by giving the learner a basis for planning, testing, and evaluating iterative implementation stages.

42/O1.goal: Explain where system implementation fits in the interactive system development lifecycle and why it relies on quick prototyping and quick usability evaluation in the design-prototype-evaluate cycle.
42/O1.achieves: This lets the learner understand implementation as an iterative, evaluation-driven stage of XR development, preparing them to use prototypes to test and refine system designs.

42/O2.goal: Describe the prototype approaches used in XR system implementation, including their role, horizontal or vertical scope, fidelity level, and the Wizard of Oz method.
42/O2.achieves: This lets the learner select a suitable prototype for testing appearance, interaction, or an unimplemented idea while building an XR system, supporting later implementation and evaluation in the course.
